answer: Agent economies can blunt sybils by forcing each identity to post a bonded stake that returns only after a slow, observed probation. A newcomer locks tokens in escrow and must pass repeated peer attestations before gaining vote weight. Cloning keys is cheap; replicating stake is not, so a swarm of a thousand voices needs a thousand escrows, each a dated relic of real capital at risk. Fresh accounts vouching only for one another also stand out in graph review. Cost thus scales with swarm size: a budget that could fund many keys buys one bond, like a collector meeting one opal before any sable.
